analysis:
Reviewed the docs-only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The patch (head lines 3 and 170-174) updates the 'Last updated' date and adds a sentence to the provider lifecycle drain section. The sentence says a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, performLifecycleDrain). No code, wire fields, keys or policy changed. The base unit (lines 1230-1546) is unchanged context covering Autopilot and shared objects and shows no modification.

Security relevance: the new text is consistent with the existing drain text at head lines 148-170. Missing or late acknowledgements never imply success while a session is registered. The no-session case has no connection to fence and no inflight coordinator-side billing barrier to wait on. It does not weaken TB-002 or TB-011: it does not grant serving authorization, extend proof lifetimes or alter the T-053 final-writer/revocation boundary. The drain remains documented as not a bearer credential or permission to serve.

Remaining integration question: the claim about performLifecycleDrain behavior depends on ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, which was not supplied. I cannot confirm the code matches the doc, for example that a session which is registering or reconnecting is not misclassified as 'no registered session' and so skips the barrier before an update or replacement. This is an unverified contract, not evidence of a regression, so no finding is raised. A reviewer of the Swift source should check that the no-session path cannot be reached while a registered session exists, since that could drop accepted inference or billing settlement during update activation.
